topics.title: Volume 2 mistake?
topics.text:
In section 16.3, exercise 16-5 part 3, it says prove that $F_0 + F_2 + F_4 + \cdots F_{2n} = F_{2n+1}$.



The solution is



[quote=AoPS]$F_{2n+1}=F_{2n} + F_{2n-1} = F_{2n} + F_{2n-2} + F_{2n-3} = F_{2n} + F_{2n-2}+F_{2n-4} + F_{2n-5} + \cdots = F_{2n} + F_{2n-2}+\cdots F_{2} + F_{0}$.[/quote]



This solution is wrong because if we plug in $n=0$, we have $F_{0} = F_{1}$ which is clearly not true because $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$.



Also, if we subtract $F_{2n}$ and then $F_{2n-2}$ on and on, we get $F_0 = F_1$ which is again, not true.

$F_k$ is the kth Fibonacci number.



Is this because I have the 7th edition and the problem might have been changed?

topics.title: Mathcounts algebra question
topics.text:
Hey. I was working on a question and got stuck on a question once I got to the systems. Could someone show me how to solve the system I listed in what I have done so far.



Question: For integers a, b, c, and d, $(x^2 + ax + b)(x^2+ cx + d) = x^4 + x^3 - 2x^2 + 17x - 5$. What is the value of $a + b + c + d?$



What I have done so far:

I got the following equations from finding the coefficient for each term.

$bd = -5$

$ac + b + d = -2$

$ad + bc = 17$

$c + a = 1$



b has to be either -5 or -1 or 5 or 1 and that means d has to be the opposite value that satisfies the first equation.



I also know the answer has to be one of the following because those are the only two possible solutions when adding up the numbers. For example: plugging in -5 for b would mean d had to be 1 and since we already know a + c is 1 we know that if b was -5 the answer would be -3. Same goes if b was any of the other numbers.



-3 or 5



A reason or hint why only 7 or only -3 would work would be appreciated as well as other solutions to the question.

Thanks

-Kman

Solution 1All that matters is the ordering of the numbers. There are $3!=6$ orderings and $2$ of them in which $x$ is the smallest. Thus the desired probability is $1-\frac{2}{6}=\frac{2}{3}$.




Solution 2First choose $x$. If $x$ is the smallest, then $y$ and $z$ both have to be greater than $x$, and each happens with probability $\frac{1}{2}$. Thus the desired probability is $1-\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{4}$.




Which solution(s) is/are incorrect?
